name: Citation Metadata
description: Core information used to identify, describe, and cite a dataset.

fields.name: Title
fields.definition: The main title of the Dataset

fields.name: Subtitle
fields.definition: A secondary title that amplifies or states certain limitations on the main title

fields.name: Alternative Title
fields.definition: Either 1) a title commonly used to refer to the Dataset or 2) an abbreviation of the main title

fields.name: Alternative URL
fields.definition: Another URL where one can view or access the data in the Dataset, e.g. a project or personal webpage

fields.name: Other Identifier Agency
fields.definition: The name of the agency that generated the other identifier

fields.name: Other Identifier Identifier
fields.definition: Another identifier uniquely identifies the Dataset

fields.name: Author Name
fields.definition: The name of the author, such as the person's name or the name of an organization

fields.name: Author Affiliation
fields.definition: The name of the entity affiliated with the author, e.g. an organization's name

fields.name: Author Identifier Type
fields.definition: The type of identifier that uniquely identifies the author (e.g. ORCID, ISNI)

fields.name: Author Identifier
fields.definition: Uniquely identifies the author when paired with an identifier type

fields.name: Point of Contact Name
fields.definition: The name of the point of contact, e.g. the person's name or the name of an organization

fields.name: Point of Contact Affiliation
fields.definition: The name of the entity affiliated with the point of contact, e.g. an organization's name

fields.name: Point of Contact E-mail
fields.definition: The point of contact's email address

fields.definition: A summary describing the purpose, nature, and scope of the Dataset

fields.name: Description Date
fields.definition: The date when the description was added to the Dataset. If the Dataset contains more than one description, e.g. the data producer supplied one description and the data repository supplied another, this date is used to distinguish between the descriptions

fields.name: Subject
fields.definition: The area of study relevant to the Dataset

fields.name: Keyword Term
fields.definition: A key term that describes important aspects of the Dataset

fields.name: Keyword Term URI
fields.definition: A URI that points to the web presence of the Keyword Term

fields.name: Keyword Controlled Vocabulary Name
fields.definition: The controlled vocabulary used for the keyword term (e.g. LCSH, MeSH)

fields.name: Keyword Controlled Vocabulary URL
fields.definition: The URL where one can access information about the term's controlled vocabulary

fields.name: Topic Classification Term
fields.definition: A topic or subject term

fields.name: Topic Classification Controlled Vocabulary Name

name: Social Science and Humanities Metadata
description: Study design, data collection methodology, and population concepts used in social science and humanities research.

fields.name: Unit of Analysis
fields.definition: Basic unit of analysis or observation that this Dataset describes, such as individuals, families/households, groups, institutions/organizations, administrative units, and more. For information about the DDI's controlled vocabulary for this element, please refer to the DDI web page at http://www.ddialliance.org/controlled-vocabularies.

fields.name: Universe
fields.definition: Description of the population covered by the data in the file; the group of people or other elements that are the object of the study and to which the study results refer. Age, nationality, and residence commonly help to  delineate a given universe, but any number of other factors may be used, such as age limits, sex, marital status, race, ethnic group, nationality, income, veteran status, criminal convictions, and more. The universe may consist of elements other than persons, such as housing units, court cases, deaths, countries, and so on. In general, it should be possible to tell from the description of the universe whether a given individual or element is a member of the population under study. Also known as the universe of interest, population of interest, and target population.

fields.name: Time Method
fields.definition: The time method or time dimension of the data collection, such as panel, cross-sectional, trend, time- series, or other.

fields.name: Data Collector
fields.definition: Individual, agency or organization responsible for  administering the questionnaire or interview or compiling the data.

fields.name: Collector Training
fields.definition: Type of training provided to the data collector

fields.name: Frequency
fields.definition: If the data collected includes more than one point in time, indicate the frequency with which the data was collected; that is, monthly, quarterly, or other.

fields.name: Sampling Procedure
fields.definition: Type of sample and sample design used to select the survey respondents to represent the population. May include reference to the target sample size and the sampling fraction.

fields.name: Target Sample Size Actual
fields.definition: Actual sample size.

fields.name: Target Sample Size Formula
fields.definition: Formula used to determine target sample size.

fields.name: Major Deviations for Sample Design
fields.definition: Show correspondence as well as discrepancies between the sampled units (obtained) and available statistics for the population (age, sex-ratio, marital status, etc.) as a whole.

fields.name: Collection Mode
fields.definition: Method used to collect the data; instrumentation characteristics (e.g., telephone interview, mail questionnaire, or other).

fields.name: Type of Research Instrument
fields.definition: Type of data collection instrument used. Structured indicates an instrument in which all respondents are asked the same questions/tests, possibly with precoded answers. If a small portion of such a questionnaire includes open-ended questions, provide appropriate comments. Semi-structured indicates that the research instrument contains mainly open-ended questions. Unstructured indicates that in-depth interviews were conducted.

fields.name: Characteristics of Data Collection Situation
fields.definition: Description of noteworthy aspects of the data collection situation. Includes information on factors such as cooperativeness of respondents, duration of interviews, number of call backs, or similar.

fields.name: Actions to Minimize Losses
fields.definition: Summary of actions taken to minimize data loss. Include information on actions such as follow-up visits, supervisory checks, historical matching, estimation, and so on.

fields.name: Control Operations
fields.definition: Control OperationsMethods to facilitate data control performed by the primary investigator or by the data archive.

fields.name: Weighting
fields.definition: The use of sampling procedures might make it necessary to apply weights to produce accurate statistical results. Describes the criteria for using weights in analysis of a collection. If a weighting formula or coefficient was developed, the formula is provided, its elements are defined, and it is indicated how the formula was applied to the data.

fields.name: Cleaning Operations
fields.definition: Methods used to clean the data collection, such as consistency checking, wildcode checking, or other.

fields.name: Study Level Error Notes
fields.definition: Note element used for any information annotating or clarifying the methodology and processing of the study.

fields.name: Response Rate
fields.definition: Percentage of sample members who provided information.

fields.name: Estimates of Sampling Error
fields.definition: Measure of how precisely one can estimate a population value from a given sample.

fields.name: Other Forms of Data Appraisal
fields.definition: Other issues pertaining to the data appraisal. Describe issues such as response variance, nonresponse rate  and testing for bias, interviewer and response bias, confidence levels, question bias, or similar.

fields.name: Source
fields.definition: Source - This describes the source of the data. Is it from the Bureau of Labor and Statistics? Is it data from the United Nations?

fields.name: Dates - Additional Information
fields.definition: Dates - Additional Information - Note any additional information about dates or time periods in the dataset including intervals (annual, decennial, centennial, etc.) Also note the column(s) in the dataset where dates and other temporal information can be found.

fields.name: Variables
fields.definition: Variables - Define the variables in this dataset. Please note the column in the dataset where variable information can be found.

fields.name: Classification Schema
fields.definition: Classification Schema - If there is a classification scheme in this dataset, please describe it. For example, M_20_24 should be read as Males, aged 20-24.

fields.name: Provenance

Since that time, the data has not been altered other than to migrate it to more current formats."

name: HEAL metadata schema
description: NIH HEAL Initiative study registration, translational focus, and data-sharing metadata.

fields.name: HEAL metadata ClinicalTrials.gov Study ID
fields.definition: ClinicalTrials.gov study ID; only applicable if study is a reportable clinical trial and registered on ClinicalTrials.gov.

fields.name: HEAL metadata CEDAR Study-level Metadata Template Instance ID
fields.definition: ID of the CEDAR HEAL Study-level Core Metadata Template instance created for this study.

fields.name: Data repositories Name of Repository
fields.definition: Name of a repository in which data or other shareable research products are submitted for storage by study author

fields.name: Data repositories Study ID assigned by Repository
fields.definition: Unique identifier assigned to the study at that repository; usually a number or combination of standard letters and numbers (e.g. study identifiers on ClinicalTrials.gov are generally in the format: NCT12345678)

fields.name: Data repositories Repository-branded Study Persistent Identifier
fields.definition: Unique persistent identifier assigned to the study at that repository; usually a doi

fields.name: Data repositories Study citation at Repository
fields.definition: The official citation the repository requests be used to cite the study/data when the study/data is discovered/accessed via the repository; will likely follow the format: Principal Investigator(s). Title. Place-of-Distribution and Distributor, Date-of-Distribution. DOI. version (where distributor will be the repository name)

fields.name: HEAL citation Name of the study group or collection(s) to which this study belongs
fields.definition: If this study belongs to a study group or collection(s), this is the name or identifier of the study group or collection(s) (e.g. SAMHSA performs a survey called the National Survey of Substance Abuse Treatment Services (N-SSATS) every year; each annual survey may be registered as a separate study that belongs to a collection called the N-SSATS collection).

fields.name: HEAL citation HEAL-branded Study Persistent Identifier
fields.definition: Persistent identifier assigned to the study on the HEAL Platform; probably a HEAL Platform-branded doi.

fields.name: HEAL citation Study citation on HEAL Platform
fields.definition: The official citation the HEAL Platform will request be used to cite the study/data when the study/data is discovered/accessed via the Platform; will likely follow the format: Principal Investigator(s). Title. Place-of-Distribution and Distributor, Date-of-Distribution. DOI. version (where distributor will be: Platform via [Repository Name]).

fields.name: HEAL citation Is this study HEAL-funded?
fields.definition: Whether or not the study is funded by the NIH HEAL initiative.

fields.name: HEAL citation Does this study belong to a study group or collection?
fields.definition: Whether or not the study is related to a study group or collection(s) by some administrative mechanism, or belongs to a group or collection of studies (e.g. SAMHSA performs a survey called the National Survey of Substance Abuse Treatment Services (N-SSATS) every year; each annual survey may be registered as a separate study that belongs to a collection called the N-SSATS collection).

fields.name: HEAL platform registrant First name of study registrant
fields.definition: First name of study registrant

fields.name: HEAL platform registrant Middle initial of study registrant
fields.definition: Middle initial of study registrant

fields.name: HEAL platform registrant Last name of study registrant
fields.definition: Last name of study registrant

fields.name: HEAL platform registrant Institutional affiliation of study registrant
fields.definition: Institutional affiliation of study registrant

fields.name: HEAL platform registrant Institutional email of study registrant
fields.definition: Institutional email of study registrant

fields.name: Data availability Will the study collect or produce data?
fields.definition: Indicate whether or not the study will collect/produce (primary or secondary) data.

fields.name: Data availability Will the study make data available?
fields.definition: If study will collect/produce data, indicate whether all, some, or none of the data will be made available.

fields.name: Data availability Will available data have restrictions on access?
fields.definition: If study will collect/produce data, and make at least some of that data available, indicate whether all, some, or none of the data will have restriction(s) on access beyond acknowledgement and signing of a minimal DSA.

fields.name: Data availability Has data collection/production started?
fields.definition: If study will collect/produce data, indicate whether the study has not started, has started, or has finished data collection/production activities.

fields.name: Data availability Has data release started?
fields.definition: If the study will collect/produce data and make at least some of the data available, indicate whether the study has not started, has started, or has finished data release activities.

fields.name: Data availability Date when first data will be released(Anticipated)
fields.definition: If study will collect/produce data and make at least some of the data available, indicate the anticipated date when first data will be released.

fields.name: Data availability Date when last data will be released (Anticipated)
fields.definition: If study will produce data and make at least some of the data available, indicate the anticipated date when last data will be released (data release is complete).

fields.name: Data availability Indicate whether or not the study will produce shareable products other than data
fields.definition: Indicate whether or not the study will produce shareable products other than data

fields.name: Findings Primary Study Findings
fields.definition: Simple, one-sentence take-away conclusion(s) from study author publications; one item in this array per single-sentence conclusion (e.g. item #1: Provision of MAT rx to men with documented OUD leaving jail reduces overdose risk by 9%; item #2: Provision of MAT rx plus case management support to men with documented OUD leaving jail reduces overdose risk by 30%; item 3: Provision of MAT rx plus case management support to men with documented OUD leaving jail is more effective than provision of MAT rx alone at reducing risk of OUD overdose).

fields.name: Findings Secondary Publications DOI
fields.definition: List of the doi for any/all secondary study publications that use the study data; include any papers, books, articles, blog posts, etc. authored by persons OTHER THAN the investigators or team responsible for the study; one item in this array per publication/doi.

fields.name: Study Translational Focus
fields.definition: Whether the study is primarily focused on learning more about a human opioid or pain CONDITION or on discovering, or learning more about a TREATMENT, intervention, or solution for a human opioid or pain condition. This may be quite simple to infer for human subject studies. For studies not involving human subjects, please consider how/where the study will most substantially contribute to the HEAL Initiative translational purpose of learning more about human opioid and pain conditions and driving development of solutions to these conditions. Choose one.

fields.name: Study Translational Focus Types of determinants/mechanisms the study is investigating
fields.definition: What types of determinants and/or mechanisms related to human opioid use or pain conditions is the study investigating and/or measuring (e.g. A study investigating differential pain/nociception signaling in persons living in neighborhoods with high versus low social cohesion might choose both 'Biology and Health' and 'Social Determinants'). Choose as many as apply.

fields.name: Study type Category or Type/Stage of Study Research
fields.definition: The high-level category or type/stage of research being conducted.

fields.name: Study type Study Type/Design
fields.definition: The overarching study type and more granular study design. Choose as many as apply.
values: Clinical Research - Therapy/drug study without intervention
Clinical Research - Case Report or Series

fields.name: Study type Is the study conducting primary or secondary research?
fields.definition: Is the study collecting data itself to analyze and draw conclusions or is it leveraging data collected by other entities to analyze and draw conclusions.

fields.name: Study type Is the study conducting observational or experimental research?
fields.definition: Whether the study is observational (no explicit intervention) or experimental (some explicit intervention).

fields.name: Study type Study Subject Type
fields.definition: What is the actual species or entity that is experimentally or observationally studied in the research; each HEAL study will have translational relevance to humans, but not all HEAL studies directly study humans.

fields.name: Human treatment applicability Treatment Investigation Stage or Type
fields.definition: If the study is investigating a treatment, intervention, or solution to a human opioid or pain condition, what type of investigation is the study undertaking? at what stage in the treatment investigation process does this study lie?

fields.name: Human treatment applicability Treatment Mode - Preventive, Therapeutic, Harm Reduction
fields.definition: the treatment, intervention, or solution that my study is relevant to meant to prevent the occurrance of a condition (e.g. development of a non-opioid drug for pain to prevent opioid exposure and addiction, case management and MAT for pregnant women to prevent in utero exposure to opioids, safe needle exchange center to prevent spread of blood borne diseases among people using heroin), treat an occurrance of a condition (e.g. naloxone to treat opioid overdose, physical therapy to treat existing pain from a back injury) , and/or is it a harm reduction mechanism (e.g. safe needle exchange reduces harm associated with heroin addiction/use, decriminalization of heroin possession or use reduces the harm associated with heroin addiction/use).
values: Harm Reduction (preventing more of an occurrence, or preventing harm from an occurrence)

fields.name: Human treatment applicability Treatment novelty
fields.definition: Is the treatment, intervention, or solution that my study is relevant to totally novel, is it totally established, does it have some element of novelty added to an established intervention (novel added to established, established used in a novel population, setting, or combination)? .
values: Established, used in novel population, setting, or combination

fields.name: Human treatment applicability Treatment Type
fields.definition: Classify the treatment, intervention, or solution the study is relevant to by broad type of intervention. Choose as many as apply.

fields.name: Human treatment applicability Is the Treatment given/applied to individuals or populations?
fields.definition: Is the treatment, intervention, or solution that my study is relevant to applied at the individual level (e.g. a doctor prescribes a drug or physical therapy regimen to a patient) or at the population/community/group level (e.g. a city changes good samaritan naloxone laws, or implements a safe needle exchange center, or adds park maintenance resources to the budget to provide more access to outside places to exercise)?

fields.name: Human condition applicability Relevant Opioid use and/or Pain condition - Category(ies)
fields.definition: Considering the study in a translational context, to humans with which broad category(ies) of opioid use or pain conditions are the study results intended to apply. Choose as many as apply
values: Opioid use and opioid use disorder
Opioid use and opioid use disorder, primary occurrence
Opioid use and opioid use disorder, relapse
Opioid use and opioid use disorder, chronic
Co-occurring (Opioid or Non-opioid) Substance use and Mental Health disorder

fields.name: Human condition applicability Opioid use and/or Pain condition - Investigation Stage or Type
fields.definition: Each HEAL study will be doing work that is relevant to a human opioid and/or pain condition. What does this study intend to learn about the condition? If the study is investigating a treatment, intervention, or solution, please choose 'Treatment of Condition'. Choose as many as apply
values: Public attitudes towards or perception of condition

fields.name: Human condition applicability Pain - Causal condition
fields.definition: If the study will be doing work that is relevant to a human PAIN condition category, is the study focusing on pain caused by a specific condition? e.g. Cancer, fibromyalgia, arthritis, occupational injury, sports injury, car accident, surgical procedure. If yes, please indicate the causal condition(s) here - Values will be restricted to NLM MeSH Diseases - see Branch 'C' here: https://meshb-prev.nlm.nih.gov/treeView.

fields.name: Human condition applicability Pain - Study treatment or target condition is causal condition or pain?
fields.definition: If the study will be doing work that is relevant to a human PAIN condition category, and the pain condition has a causal condition (specified above), is the study focusing its investigation on the causal condition, or on the pain resulting from the causal condition? e.g. In a study of effective treatments for fibromyalgia/fibromyalgia pain, is the study focused on fibromyalgia disease-modifying treatments, or on treatments that address the symptomology of pain? Choose as many as apply.

fields.name: Human condition applicability Study treatment or target condition - Detail
fields.definition: Considering the study in a translational context, to humans with which detailed type of opioid use or pain conditions are the study results intended to apply? Each HEAL study will be doing work that is relevant to a human opioid and/or pain condition; You indicated the broad category of condition(s) the study is focusing on or relevant to above. Here, please indicate the study focus condition(s) in detail. Choose as many as apply - Values will be restricted to NLM MeSH Diseases - see Branch 'C' here: https://meshb-prev.nlm.nih.gov/treeView.

fields.name: Human condition applicability Study outcome condition - Detail
fields.definition: If the outcome condition(s) the study hopes to impact or measure is different than the treatment or study target condition (e.g. testing a disease-modifying fibromyaligia treatment but measuring depression, physical and social function, and neurologic pain such as headaches as the main outcomes). Please indicate the study outcome condition(s) here. Choose as many as apply - Values will be restricted to NLM MeSH Diseases - see Branch 'C' here: https://meshb-prev.nlm.nih.gov/treeView.

fields.name: Human condition applicability Other measured or tracked conditions - Detail
fields.definition: If the study is measuring or tracking other human health conditions besides the treatment or study target condition and outcome condition, please indicate the other tracked/measured condition(s) here. Choose as many as apply - Values will be restricted to NLM MeSH Diseases - see Branch 'C' here: https://meshb-prev.nlm.nih.gov/treeView.

fields.name: Human subject applicability To humans of which gender identity(ies) do study results apply?
fields.definition: Considering the study in a translational context, to humans of which gender identity(ies) are the study results intended to apply and/or likely to generalize to.

fields.name: Human subject applicability To humans of which sexual identity(ies) do study results apply?
fields.definition: Considering the study in a translational context, to humans of which sexual identity(ies) are the study results intended to apply and/or likely to generalize to.

fields.name: Human subject applicability To humans of which age/developmental stage do study results apply?
fields.definition: Considering the study in a translational context, to humans of which age or developmental stage are the study results intended to apply and/or likely to generalize to.
values: Aged, 80 and over (80 years and over)

fields.name: Human subject applicability To humans in which special vulnerability categories do study results apply?
fields.definition: Considering the study in a translational context, which special IRB human vulnerability conditions are the study results intended to address or apply to?
values: Individuals with mental disabilities or cognitive impairments
Institutionalized persons (for example, persons in correctional facilities, nursing homes or mental health facilities)

fields.name: Human subject applicability To humans of which geographic area do study results apply?
fields.definition: For studies with human subjects, from which geographic location(s) are subjects recruited. If subjects are recruited in the US nationally, choose only US - national. If subject are recruited in the US only in specific state(s), choose US - Specific States, then please also select the abbreviation of each of the specific states from which subjects are recruited. If subjects are recruited in the US from specific county(ies) within specific state(s), please choose US - Specific States and US - Specific Counties, and choose the abbreviation of each specific state from which subjects are recruited

fields.name: Data Is data quantitative or qualitative?
fields.definition: Does the study produce/collect quantitative data?, qualitative data? Choose as many as apply.

fields.name: Data Source of Data
fields.definition: What is the source of the data the study will produce/collect. Choose as many as apply

fields.name: Data Type of Data
fields.definition: What is the type of the data the study will produce/collect. Choose as many as apply.

fields.name: Data Human Subject Data - Unit of Collection
fields.definition: For studies with human subjects, is the data collected at the individual or population level?

fields.name: Data Human Subject Data - Expected Number of the Unit of Collection
fields.definition: For studies with human subjects, what is the expected number of subjects for which data will be collected? If unit of data collection is individuals this is the expected number of individuals, and if the unit of data collection is populations/clusters this is the expected number of populations/clusters

fields.name: Data Human Subject Data - Unit of Analysis
fields.definition: For studies with human subjects, is the data analyzed at the individual or population level?

fields.name: Data Human Subject Data - Expected Number of the Unit of Analysis
fields.definition: For studies with human subjects, what is the expected number of subjects at the level at which data will be analyzed? If unit of data analysis is individuals this is the expected number of individuals, and if the unit of data analysis is populations/clusters this is the expected number of populations/clusters.

fields.name: Data Human Subject Data - Individual or Aggregated Data made available?
fields.definition: For studies with human subjects that will make at least some data available, will data be made available at the individual subject level or some level of aggregation?

fields.name: Data Human Subject Geographic Data - Collected at what level of detail?
fields.definition: For studies with human subjects, will geographic data be collected? if so, what level of geographic detail will be collected?
values: No geographic data will be collected

fields.name: Data Human Subject Geographic Data - Available at what level of detail?
fields.definition: For studies with human subjects that collect geographic data and will make at least some data available, will geographic data be made available? if so, what level of geographic detail will be made available?
values: No geographic data will be made available
